newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices continue to strengthen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices continue to strengthen.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for November 1 delivery were steady to stronger Tuesday, with the Midcontinent and western markets led higher by forecasts for cold weather later in the week and short supplies in the Northwest, industry sources said.
November Gulf Coast prices were stable in the low-$2.70s, still up more than 80 cents from October 1 levels, as most nomination deadlines for November 1 mostly expired this morning.

While most Gulf traders had locked in their November bidweek business late Monday, Midcontinent buyers emerged again today for November 1 gas. Prices gained an additional 10-15 cents to the mid-to-high $2.60s, riding on forecasts for colder weather by Thursday throughout the central U.S.
October Midcontinent prices were similarly higher in the high-$2.60s to low-$2.70s.

In west Texas, where temperatures were also expected to dip to below-normal levels in the early part of November, traders reported closing Permian basin deals in the $2.60-2.68 range, up an additional five cents from Monday and up about a $1 from October 1 values.

November prices at the southern California border held steady in the mid-$2.70s despite continued strength in the Canadian market. Temperatures are expected to moderate Friday in the Northwest following recent significantly below-normal temperatures.

In contrast, prices on the opposite coast at the New York city-gate were tempered by mild temperatures in the Northeast. Traders reported closing deals in the low-to-mid $3.30s, down from Monday's highs of $3.50.
